source.author: verg
source.text: hic crudelis amor tauri, suppostaque furto Pasiphaë, mixtumque genus prolesque biformis Minotaurus inest, Veneris monumenta nefandae; hic labor ille domus et inextricabilis error; magnum reginae sed enim miseratus amorem Daedalus ipse dolos tecti ambagesque resolvit, caeca regens filo vestigia.
source.text_original: hic crudelis amor tauri, suppostaque furto / Pasiphaë, mixtumque genus prolesque biformis / Minotaurus inest, Veneris monumenta nefandae; / hic labor ille domus et inextricabilis error; / magnum reginae sed enim miseratus amorem / Daedalus ipse dolos tecti ambagesque resolvit, / caeca regens filo vestigia.
source.text_english: Here is the cruel love of the bull, and Pasiphaë brought under by stealth, and the mixed breed, the two-formed offspring Minotaurus, memorials of shameful Venus; here is that toil of the house and the inextricable error; but Daedalus himself, pitying the queen’s great love, untangled the deceits and labyrinthine windings of the building, guiding the blind footsteps with a thread.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Ita et ego istarum Scripturarum ingressus Oceanum, et mysteriorum Dei, ut sic loquar, labyrinthum, de quo scriptum est: Posuit tenebras latibulum suum; Et: Nubes in circuitu ejus: perfectam quidem scientiam veritatis mihi vindicare non audeo, sed nosse cupientibus aliqua doctrinae indicia praebuisse, non meis viribus, sed Christi misericordia, qui errantibus nobis ipse dolos tecti ambagesque resolvit, caeca regens Spiritu sancto vestigia; quem sequentes, ad portum explanationum prophetae Ezechielis pervenire poterimus, in quem extremus, id est, quartus decimus liber est.
reuse.text_original: Ita et ego istarum Scripturarum ingressus Oceanum, et mysteriorum Dei, ut sic loquar, labyrinthum, de quo scriptum est: Posuit tenebras latibulum suum; Et: Nubes in circuitu ejus: perfectam quidem scientiam veritatis mihi vindicare non audeo, sed nosse cupientibus aliqua doctrinae indicia praebuisse, non meis viribus, sed Christi misericordia, qui errantibus nobis ipse dolos tecti ambagesque resolvit, caeca regens Spiritu sancto vestigia; quem sequentes, ad portum explanationum prophetae Ezechielis pervenire poterimus, in quem extremus, id est, quartus decimus liber est.
reuse.text_english: Thus I too, having entered the ocean of these Scriptures and, so to speak, the labyrinth of God’s mysteries—of which it is written, He made darkness his hiding place; and: clouds are round about him—I do not dare claim for myself a perfect knowledge of the truth, but I have, not by my own strength but by Christ’s mercy, offered to those who desire to know some indications of doctrine; for he himself, guiding our blind steps by the Holy Spirit, untangles the concealed deceptions and winding paths. Following him, we shall be able to reach the harbor of explanations of the prophet Ezechiel, of which this is the last book, that is, the fourteenth.
